evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Joanna: 'it might take about ten to fifteen minutes if this is a good time' — framing present but no clear wait for confirmation before pivoting to 'Aside from the pricing, just want to check out if you have any other important concerns'
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Joanna: 'Aside from the pricing, just want to check out if you have any other important concerns that you also want to discuss on this call?' — asked after the time-box framing, but logically part of the open, before detailed logistics probing
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Aliano/Liana), moving day (November 13), route (1850 Mercer Parkway, Pharma Branch to 1959 Riven Lane, Louisville), size (1398 sq ft, 2 bedroom) — all four confirmed
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment/townhome), floor (ground floor with balcony access), rooms (2 bedrooms, living room, son's room), parking (front or back garage), special items (washer/dryer, TVs, desks, mini-fridge, ~40-50 boxes), stairs at destination (one flight) — seven logistics items substantially covered
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Joanna: 'you're good with packing. Like, you're planning to do all the packing yourself' — offered implicitly as 'do you want us to pack' by contrast
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: No explicit box-count range given; customer volunteered '40 to 50 boxes' but rep did not ask the typical range-anchor question
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Joanna: 'Typically a two bedroom apartment usually takes three and a half to five and a half hours...based on the items...I'm just estimating it more on the four and a half to six and a half hour mark...estimated budget of $1,443' — range provided and personalized to stairs and driving distance
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Joanna: '$111 per hour per mover...all inclusive rates...no other fees...two men and the truck, all the wraps...insurance, credit card fees, all of that is already in the price...two and a half hour minimum...only charge every fifteen minutes' — fully disclosed
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked; rep moves directly to the ask: 'would you like our help for this move'
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Joanna: 'on time guarantee if we run late on the time that we schedule we provide discounts for your move' — discount terms stated clearly
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Joanna: 'no worries, damage coverage, which would give you up to $2,000 coverage for any repair, replacement reimbursement for any accidental damages' — coverage and amount stated, but no explicit 'no deductible / no fine print' framing; no clear statement it's built into the rate
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No closing reflection or 'Does that put those to rest?' type confirmation after the Two Promises delivery
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked; call moves directly to the explicit ask without a 'What's still concerning you?' checkpoint
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Joanna: 'would you like our help for this move on that day on the Friday' — plainly asked, but immediately followed by customer hesitation. Joanna then pivots to 'I'll send you everything in an email as well...if you decide to book, you can just respond to the email or give us a call' — built-in out softens the ask
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: No booking details confirmed; customer explicitly declined to book ('I'd like to get a few more quotes before I decide'), and rep accepted with email follow-up only

top_strength: Thorough logistics probing — Joanna gathered nearly all seven detail categories (property type, floor, rooms, parking, special items, stairs, access) and personalized the estimate to stairs and driving distance, creating a credible and contextualized quote.
coaching_note: Ask 'Does that feel fair?' with genuine silence after the estimate, and do a final concerns check before the explicit ask — both are load-bearing closers that were skipped here.
